content.intro: Learn database backup and recovery through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Database Backup and Recovery matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines database backup and recovery as part of database configuration, migrations, and transactions. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Backup strategies; Logical and physical backups; Restoration procedures; Testing recovery; Coordinating schema and data recovery. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Backup strategies
items.text: Backup strategies should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

items.title: Logical and physical backups
items.text: Logical and physical backups should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

items.title: Restoration procedures
items.text: For Restoration procedures, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Testing recovery
items.text: A good test covers an observable contract and asserts status, output, database changes or access denial. Include invalid and boundary inputs so a regression does not only fail on a happy path.

items.title: Coordinating schema and data recovery
items.text: Coordinating schema and data recovery affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
